Fuel cells · Specialized / demonstration

Alkaline fuel cell · AFC

Hydroxide ions move from the oxygen electrode to the hydrogen electrode.

Animated operating principles

Ion and electron pathways

OH⁻ · electrolyte / membrane Electrons e⁻ · external circuit

Simplified reaction directions and pathways. Actual particle numbers and speeds differ.

Electrode and electrolyte principles

OH⁻ moves from the air electrode to the fuel electrode through the alkaline electrolyte.

Air electrode: ½O₂ + H₂O + 2e⁻ → 2OH⁻ / Fuel electrode: H₂ + 2OH⁻ → 2H₂O + 2e⁻

Advantages

Fast reaction kinetics with options for non-precious-metal catalysts.

Drawbacks & challenges

Sensitive to CO₂; air and electrolyte management are needed.

Materials & supply constraints

Depends on catalyst composition; platinum is not always required.

Main applications

Space and specialized power; some mobile systems
